problem:
Let $f(x,y,z)$ be a differentiable function such that

$$
f(-1,0,1)=-1,\,{f}_{x}(x,y,z)={z}^{2},\,{f}_{y}(x,y,z)=1,\,{f}_{z}(x,y,z)=2xz.
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(-1,0,1),$ estimate the value of $f(-0.95,0.02,1.04).$
worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b,c)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y,z)≈f(a,b,c)+∇f(a,b,c)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b,z-c⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(-1,0,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & ≈f(-1,0,1)+∇f(-1,0,1)\cdot ⟨x-(-1),y-0,z-1⟩ \\  & ≈-1+⟨{f}_{x}(-1,0,1),{f}_{y}(-1,0,1),{f}_{z}(-1,0,1)⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,y,z-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{x}(-1,0,1)$, ${f}_{y}(-1,0,1)$ and ${f}_{z}(-1,0,1),$ using the given partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(-1,0,1) & ={1}^{2}=1 \\ {f}_{y}(-1,0,1) & =1 \\ {f}_{z}(-1,0,1) & =2(-1)(1)=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
f(x,y,z)≈-1+⟨1,1,-2⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,y,z-1⟩.
$$

Finally, we can estimate $f(-0.95,0.02,1.04)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=-0.95,y=0.02$ and $y=1.04,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-0.95,0.02,1.04) & ≈-1+⟨1,1,-2⟩\cdot ⟨-0.95+1,0.02,1.04-1⟩ \\  & ≈-1+⟨1,1,-2⟩\cdot ⟨0.05,0.02,0.04⟩ \\  & ≈-1+1(0.05)+1(0.02)-2(0.04) \\  & ≈-1+0.05+0.02-0.08 \\  & ≈-1.01\end{aligned}
$$
